_source: Branch Education Short 'Zooming Into a CPU (It's Incredible)', watched in the built-in browser 2026-11-18: frames every ~4 s. No transcript panel, so line timings and word counts are estimated from the burned-in captions at ~150 words a minute. Our own descriptions.

hook.firstFrame: a smartphone lying on a pale grey tiled floor, soft daylight, slight tilt
hook.firstLine: Every phone has a processor made of billions of transistors

shots.picture: a phone lying on a pale grey tiled floor
the phone lifts and its layers slide apart into an exploded stack
the logic board out of the stack; a leader line labels the main chip and the bare die floats off
a fast dive down onto the die until its surface becomes a red-brown field of tiny blocks
one transistor rises out of the field as coloured blocks with a dimension bracket over it
the field turns grey; a few cells lift out in a column, labelled gate by gate, under a glowing title
rows of cells like a city from above, the camera gliding across
copper wire layers rise over the cells like a maze of beams
the wiring as a cut-away stack, a bracket counts its layers; top layers widen
the whole copper wiring block sitting on the die from a high angle
an end card: a framed thumbnail of the long video and a channel badge with arrows

lines.gist: every phone holds a processor of billions of transistors
zooming in reveals an endless field of them
each one only a few nanometres across
they are grouped into logic gates called standard cells
to connect the gates a huge maze of wires is needed
the wiring is stacked in many layers, finer at the bottom
the layers connect the whole chip; points to the long video

ending.cta: watch the long video on CPU logic
ending.lastFrame: end card with a framed thumbnail and channel badge over a dimmed shot

whyItWorks: one unbroken zoom from a phone on the floor to a single transistor, each scale labelled as it passes
an exploded view in the first 3 seconds: the phone's layers slide apart so the chip is found, not cut to
measurements drawn as brackets on the 3D part itself (nanometres, layer counts) rather than on cards
parts lift out of a field with a shadow below and a label on a leader line, then sink back
